title: INT-03 · Diplomacy: Summits, Communications, Joint Declarations

blocks.text: Diplomacy uses a coded language. A ‘frank’ meeting is one in which the parties disagree; ‘agreeing to continue consultations’ often means that no agreement has been reached; and ‘expresses concern’, ‘condemns’ and ‘strongly condemns’ sit at distinct points on a scale. Anyone reading open sources needs to understand this code without exaggerating or overlooking its nuances. In this unit, you will learn the vocabulary of visits and summits, the ‘thermometer’ of diplomatic adjectives, the scale of verbs used in communiqués and resolutions, the structure of a joint statement (including clauses introduced by ⁧إِذْ⁩ ), diplomatic actions (summoning an ambassador, recalling one, severing relations) and how to read what a communiqué leaves unsaid. The sources in the texts are fictional; the writing exercise uses a real public communiqué. Two weeks.

rows: INT-01 (assignment, prudence); INT-02 (institutions, securities); B2-03 (political lexicon); B2-06

blocks.text: Materials This unit, official sites in Arabic (for the exercise 11), session with the tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. understand news about visits, talks and summits and their fixed formulas;
2. interpret the adjectives of the diplomatic thermometer and make them in English without exaggerating or mitigating;
3. recognize the scale of verbs in a statement or resolution (from ⁧يُرَحِّبُ⁩ a ⁧يُدِينُ بِشِدَّةٍ⁩ );
4. read the structure of a joint declaration: preamble by ⁧إِذْ⁩ and device;
5. note what a statement fails to say and report it with caution.
